test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In following figure, XA is parallel to PQ . What is the value (in degrees) of angle YBP ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4b82621a348452b4bd68e27047086168b61c5128efe128032afef5d8c581d58.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal.

Identify XA || PQ and transversal line YB.

⇒ ∠YBP and ∠XAY are corresponding angles.

⇒ ∠YBP = ∠XAY = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** XA || PQ and ∠XAY = 80°.

**Formula Used:** Corresponding Angles Property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/373c172751dffed48ed40574780ea57394cbc8e6dfc1b910a3b8c93f79cec826.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Line XA is parallel to Line PQ (XA || PQ).

⇒ The line YB acts as a transversal intersecting XA at A and PQ at B.

⇒ ∠XAY and ∠YBP are located in the same relative position at each intersection.

⇒ According to the Corresponding Angles Theorem, ∠YBP = ∠XAY.

⇒ Since ∠XAY = 80°, then ∠YBP = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. If the two lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal. These angles are always equal (e.g., ∠XAB = ∠ABQ).

Co-interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal and inside the parallel lines. Their sum is always 180° (∠XAB + ∠ABP = 180°).
